newsitem.title: UK: Relax, don't panic, UK's Clarke tells rival Blair.
newsitem.headline: Relax, don't panic, UK's Clarke tells rival Blair.

text.p: Britain's Conservative finance minister Kenneth Clarke offered some advice to opposition Labour leader Tony Blair on Friday -- stop panicking, relax and act like a statesman.

Clarke, the Chancellor of the Exchequer, told a caller to a BBC television phone-in programme that he did not believe opinion polls giving Labour a lead of 20 points or more over the Conservatives ahead of the May 1 election.

"I think he might lose. Looking at Tony, one of the things that worries me about the way he's fighting this campaign -- and I shouldn't say this in this friendly way -- is I can't understand why he does appear to be panicking and saying the first thing that comes off the top of his head," Clarke said.

"It's a very worrying sign if he does that under the pressure of an election campaign when he ought to be confident, relaxed. He believes the polls. He ought to think -- 20 percent ahead. Why can't he start practising being statesmanlike?"
Clarke said Blair was trying to frighten old people by falsely accusing the Conservatives of planning to abolish state pensions.
"Personally, I think the polls are wrong. Every candidate I meet who, like me, has done some campaigning, thinks it's nothing like as bad as the polls are saying," the Chancellor added.
